memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the north side their boundary began at the Jordan, passed the northern slope of Jericho and headed west into the hill country, coming out at the wilderness of Beth Aven. From there it crossed to the south slope of Luz (that is, Bethel) and continued down to Ataroth Addar on the hill south of Lower Beth Horon. From the hill facing Beth Horon on the south the boundary turned south along the western side and came out at Kiriath Baal (that is, Kiriath Jearim), a town of the people of Judah. This was the western side - Josh 18:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The borders of Benjamin are traced carefully — the northern slope of Jericho, the hill country, Bethel, Beth Horon. Among these place names is Bethel, "the house of God," where centuries earlier Jacob had dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven and heard God renew His promises (Gen 28:12-15). The land Benjamin inherits is soaked in the memory of God's faithfulness to their ancestors.

There is something moving in receiving an inheritance that includes such places. Every time a Benjamite passed near Bethel, they could remember: here God met our forefather Jacob; here He promised to be with him and keep him wherever he went. The geography itself preached God's faithfulness across the generations. The past mercies of God were built into the very ground they now called home.

We too can find our present blessings soaked in the memory of God's past faithfulness. The places and seasons where God has met us become markers we return to, reminders that the God who was faithful then is faithful still. Jacob's ladder at Bethel pointed forward to something greater — Jesus Himself, the true ladder between heaven and earth, through whom God comes down to us and we are brought up to God (John 1:51). The house of God is no longer a place but a Person, and in Him we find our lasting inheritance.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "Bethel" places or seasons remind you of God's faithfulness?
- How does remembering God's past mercies strengthen your present faith?
- What does it mean that Jesus is the true ladder between heaven and earth?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for the places and seasons where You have met me. Let the memory of Your faithfulness strengthen me, and thank You for Jesus, who joins heaven and earth. Amen.
